title: Consolidated after-action: RBACv2/audit SLO reconciliation & alert rework after SSO failover incident
creator: Evelyn Park
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 22:47 UTC we observed a customer-impacting SSO failover event that surfaced as two symptoms: elevated auth latency and a significant gap in audit log coverage for administrative actions across several orgs. Initial triage indicated RBACv2 cache staleness combined with the audit ingestion pipeline hitting a sampling/throttling threshold during the failover window. Missing audit entries caused compliance risk for some customers and made incident triage more difficult.

Why this ticket exists:
This ticket consolidates the engineering follow-ups across RBACv2, audit-logging, SSO failover hardening, and alerts/SLOs. It captures the decisions from the post-incident review, proposed mitigations, owner assignments, and instrumentation changes required to both prevent recurrence and reduce median time to recovery in future incidents.

Incident timeline (abridged):
- 2026-03-09 22:47 UTC: Primary SSO provider entered brief degraded mode; automated failover to backup triggered.
- 22:48–22:55 UTC: Spike in auth latencies (p95->p99) as session/token validation hit edge cases.
- 22:50–23:10 UTC: Audit ingestion pipeline logged 40% sampling drop due to backpressure on the collector; retention policy further discarded some messages before persistent storage.
- 23:15 UTC: First customer report about missing admin action logs; ops began correlation.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- RBACv2 cache invalidation policy did not anticipate concurrent SSO failovers; cached role bindings could be stale for up to 45s while the cache reconciler waited for scheduled refresh (race with token re-issuance).
- Audit pipeline had a backpressure behavior that, under high ingest lip bursts, switched to an aggressive sampling mode without emitting a clear metric/alert.
- Console-side observability lacked a single panel showing "audit coverage delta" vs expected event rate, making the gap invisible to SREs until customers reported it.

Decisions and trade-offs made during review:
- Short-term: prioritize a targeted RBACv2 cache invalidation patch that reduces worst-case staleness to <5s at the cost of slightly higher reconciliation load during failovers. Trade-off: higher CPU during failovers vs unacceptable missing logs/compliance exposure.
- Long-term: re-architect audit ingestion handshake so that sampling never silently increases without an explicit error metric. This will be a larger effort and scoped for runtime-1.25.
- Observability: add an "audit drop rate" alert with a >1% sustained deviation threshold (5m window) and an SLO/alert for cumulative missing admin events per org.

Action plan (owners + deliverables):
1) RBACv2 cache hardening (owner: Marcus Lee) — due 2026-03-21
   - Implement immediate patch: aggressive invalidation on SSO failover signal (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbactools/pull/1849).
   - Add integration test simulating concurrent token rotation + role change. CI job: integration/auth-cache-failover.

2) Audit pipeline stabilization (owner: Priya Nambiar) — due 2026-03-28
   - Disable silent sampling fallback; require explicit backpressure metric before any sampling change (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-ingest/pull/672).
   - Increase temporary retention of raw audit buffer from 1h->6h for bursts and add replay path.

3) Observability & Alerts (owner: Aisha Kumar) — due 2026-03-18
   - New dashboard: "Auth & Audit Health" (Grafana link: https://grafana.redwood-inference.net/d/auth-audit/health).
   - Alerts: audit_drop_rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> Severity P1, tag on-call SRE and security-oncall.
   - Add SLO reconciliation job that daily compares expected vs ingested admin events and creates a ticket if deviation >0.5%.

4) Runbook and Console UX (owner: Daniel Rossi) — due 2026-03-25
   - Update runbook: add step to check "audit coverage delta" and manual replay instructions.
   - Console: small UX change to surface recent audit gaps on org settings page (design/PR in drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1AuthAuditConsole).

5) Compliance & customer outreach (owner: Mariana Silva) — due 2026-03-16
   - Prepare customer impact notes and remediation timeline for affected orgs.
   - Coordinate legal/security review (ticket: https://confluence.redwood-inference.net/display/SEC/SSO+Failover+March+2026).

Instrumentation & metric changes required:
- New metrics: auth.cache_staleness_seconds (gauge), audit.ingest_sample_rate (gauge), audit.drop_rate_by_org (counter-derived).
- Existing metric reuses: auth.latency_p99 tagged by failover=true, audit.ingest_backpressure_events.
- Logging: add structured field audit.outcome and include event_id for guaranteed correlation across services.

Follow-up meetings and checkpoints:
- 2026-03-12: Internal postmortem sync (notes in Confluence).
- Weekly checkpoints on Monday cycle calls until all action items are closed.

Links to artifacts:
- Postmortem notes: https://confluence.redwood-inference.net/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=SSO-Failover-2026-03
- Incident timeline & raw logs: https://internal-logs.redwood-inference.net/incident/2026-03-09-sso-failover
- PRs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rbactools/pull/1849, https://github.com/redwood-inference/audit-ingest/pull/672
- Dashboard (Auth & Audit Health): https://grafana.redwood-inference.net/d/auth-audit/health

Acceptance criteria for this ticket (all must be satisfied):
- RBACv2 worst-case cache staleness reduced to <5s for failover scenarios (validated by integration test + canary run).
- Audit ingestion no longer performs silent sampling; backpressure events must be exposed via metric and generate an alert.
- New "audit coverage delta" dashboard panels added and alert firing in staging.
- Updated runbook and console note published; security review completed.

Risks and monitoring after deploy:
- Risk: more aggressive cache invalidation could increase CPU and produce transient auth latencies for a small percentage of requests — mitigated by canary and autoscaling adjustments on deploy.
- Monitoring: we will run elevated retention + verbose logging for 72 hours post-deploy and review with security/ops.

Next steps (short):
- Marcus to merge RBAC patch behind a feature flag and run canary (ETA 3/17).
- Priya to deploy audit-ingest changes to staging and validate no silent sampling (ETA 3/18).
- Aisha to create alert and dashboard tiles in staging; link the alert to the runbook (ETA 3/16).

If you are assigned an action above, update this ticket with PR links, test evidence, and any surprising trade-offs. For blockers, tag #security and paging SRE as needed.
